title: De Minaur haunted by Montreal Masters double-fault drama

Alex de Minaur let things slip from a winning position against Cameron Norrie to bow out of the Canadian Open. (AP: The Canadian Press/Christinne Muschi)

Australia's Alex de Minaur has let a big opportunity slip at the Canadian Open, losing to Britain's Cameron Norrie after holding match point.

De Minaur was third seed at the Open, also known as the Montreal Masters, but he threw in two key double faults to give up the lead and lose to Norrie 5-7, 7-6 (5), 6-1.

De Minaur can only drop from seven to eight in the world rankings if Ben Shelton wins the title, which means the Aussie will keep his top-eight seeding for the US Open.

A double fault has proved costly for Alex de Minaur with the Australian star blowing a match point before falling to Briton Cameron Norrie at the Montreal Masters.

Third-seeded De Minaur was up 5-2 and 40-30 in the second set, but stumbled to allow Norrie back into their third-round match.

He had another chance when serving for the match at 5-4, but again double-faulted to surrender the game on Norrie's fourth break point.

World number 37 Norrie then dug deep to record a 5-7, 7-6 (5), 6-1 victory after two hours and 52 minutes in difficult, humid conditions.

Norrie said he had to weather de Minaur's early onslaught with the newly married Aussie starting with a bang.

"From the beginning, Alex came out firing and I was like, 'Woah, this is a crazy level', and I had to match it," Norrie said in his on-court interview.

"I managed to go up a break [in the first set], but he stayed really tough and I know he's so tough as a competitor and stole that first set.

"He was looking good in the second set, and I think he took the foot off the gas very slightly and I managed to free up, steal the tie-break and then it was just a battle.

"It was a great match to win, and to test my level and I can take so much confidence from this one."

Alex de Minaur and fellow Australians Alexei Popyrin and Tahlia Gibson all record encouraging wins three weeks out from the US Open in New York.

Entering Thursday's (Friday AEST) match, de Minaur was the highest seed remaining at the hard court tournament, also known as the Canadian Open, with defending champion and fifth seed Ben Shelton taking over that title.

In some good news for de Minaur, because American Taylor Fritz and Italian Flavio Cobolli have also exited the event early, he can only possibly drop from seven to eight in the rankings, and that's only if Shelton wins the title.

That means the Australian, who broke through for a career-high number five ranking in July, will keep his top-eight US Open seeding intact for now.

De Minaur is looking to improve on quarter-final finishes at Flushing Meadows in the past two years.

Norrie will next take on 18th seed Arthur Fils, who earlier cruised past Mariano Navone 6-3, 6-2 to maintain his impressive record at Masters 1000 events this year.
